analysis.title: The Point for Asia Pacific, Monday, 16 November 2026
key_insights: Top Call: Jensen Huang has resigned as Nvidia CEO. Nvidia named CFO Colette Kress interim CEO and said existing product commitments continue. Citi sees the main supply-chain risk as a slowdown in platform upgrades, not an immediate change in AI demand.

Citi says products in development or nearing mass production in the next 1-2 years should be relatively insulated by engineering milestones, supplier qualifications and customer commitments. Disruption to longer-term architecture and supplier coordination would complicate the outlook from 2028 onward.
Citi sees TSMC and ASEH as resilient because of customer diversity. Hon Hai is gaining share in ASICs. ASIC design service names Mediatek, GUC and Alchip may draw more investor attention.

Taiwan PCB and tech hardware: AI datacenter buildout from 2028 now faces uncertainty, US national security focus could tighten, and Nvidia's Singapore sales (22% of group sales in the quarter ended July-25) could face more scrutiny. Citi sees a more favorable trend for ASIC/AMD, less pricing upside from spec migration or supply tightness, and improving component supply for general-purpose servers and consumer electronics.
Citi's Taiwan hardware preference order is ABF (Unimicron, ZDT) > PCB (GCE, Tripod) > CCL (TUC). In ODM it likes Wiwynn (high ASIC sales mix) and Hon-Hai (diversification).

BYD (1211.HK): Citi expects 4Q26E domestic net profit per car flat to slightly up QoQ. Overseas net profit per car excluding forex has been stable at Rmb20k this year. First-gen blade battery inventory is 1.5 months.

BYD management plans to offset the reduced export tax rebate (4%) and battery consumption tax hike (2%) with price hikes on new overseas models, overseas dealer rebate adjustments (overseas 15-20% vs domestic ~5%) and supply chain cost cuts. Citi expects 4Q26E wholesales above 1.5mn units, with Nov/Dec growing MoM from October's 490k.

NAURA (002371.SZ): 3Q26 slower revenue growth came from a component supply shortage (such as MFC mass flow controllers) that is almost solved through China sourcing. Management expects revenue growth to accelerate significantly in 4Q26. New orders grew 60% YoY in 9M26 and management sees no sign of turning bearish in 2027 on demand from China's leading memory makers. Gross margin may hold at 40% because rising ASP in China is unlikely.

Busy Ming (1768.HK): 10M26 SSS still grew positively. New openings will slow in 2027E, with a likely sequential SSS recovery in 1H27E. Net cash was Rmb10.9bn at end-1H26 and operating cash flow was 1.8x YoY in 1H26. Management is willing to improve shareholder returns but has no finalized plan.

Fund flows, week of 11 November 2026: equity funds had US$98.3bn of inflows and bond funds almost none. US ETFs took in US$66.1bn and global ETFs US$15.4bn, while their non-ETFs saw redemptions. Japan ETFs drew US$20.8bn over the past 4 weeks.
Atour (ATAT.O): management expects a stable 4Q26E trend, with October-to-date trending well on resilient leisure travel and MICE demand. No specific 2027E RevPAR guidance. Citi maintains Buy.

Eicher Motors (EICH.BO): 2QFY27 results were marginally below Citi's estimates on higher other expenses and staff costs. Inventory is 7-8 days against a normal 3-4 weeks, and volumes are capacity-constrained. The second brownfield expansion module is advanced to 4QFY27 (likely Jan 2027). Only 50% of cost pressure has been passed on through price hikes. Target price is unchanged at Rs9,500.

Leeno Industrial (058470.KQ): 3Q sales fell to W82.7bn (-42% QoQ, -15% YoY) and operating profit to W39.4bn (-46% QoQ, -18% YoY) because a labor strike disrupted production. Operating margin was 48%, better than expected on favorable 2nm WMCM socket mix. Citi rates it Buy and sees near-term headwinds behind it.

SingTel (STEL.SI): 2QFY27 results showed an expected sequential moderation. Full-year OpCo EBIT growth guidance was raised to mid-to-high single digits. Optus had double-digit QoQ EBIT growth and the 1H dividend rose 10% YoY. Citi reiterates Buy and raised its target price to S$4.90 from S$4.85.

Thai Life Insurance (TLI.BK): 3Q26 VoNB rose 3% YoY to THB1,486mn despite a 19% fall in APE, on an 11.7ppt margin recovery to 54.7%. Net profit fell 19% and core profit 9% YoY. Total CSM is THB92.9bn and CAR is 464.7%.

Target price changes: Vinhomes cut to D69,105 from D83,800 (Neutral). Classys cut to W33,000 from W54,000 (Buy). Compal cut to NT$28 from NT$33 (Sell). Misto cut to W47,000 from W54,000 (Buy). EugeneTechnology cut to W158,000 from W193,000 (Buy). Grasim cut to Rs3,550 from Rs3,850 (Buy). Vodafone Idea cut to Rs16 from Rs17 (Buy).

Atour: Citi maintains Buy after a 3Q26 beat, with management expecting a stable 4Q26 trend.
Leeno: Citi keeps Buy, seeing the labor-strike hit to production behind the company and margins resilient at 48%.
Eicher: SOTP-based target price unchanged at Rs9,500 despite higher volume estimates and lower margin assumptions.

sector_views.rationale: Near-term demand is insulated by existing commitments. The risk is a slowdown in platform upgrades and uncertainty over the 2028 datacenter buildout. Citi favors diversified names such as TSMC, ASEH and Hon Hai.
Preference order is ABF (Unimicron, ZDT) > PCB (GCE, Tripod) > CCL (TUC), with less pricing upside expected from spec migration or supply tightness.

earnings_insights: Eicher Motors 2QFY27 results were marginally below Citi estimates (reported vs Citi expectations) on higher other expenses and staff costs, partly offset by better gross margin.
Leeno Industrial 3Q26 reported: sales W82.7bn (-42% QoQ, -15% YoY), operating profit W39.4bn (-46% QoQ, -18% YoY), operating margin 48%, better than expected.

SingTel 2QFY27 reported: underlying NPAT fell QoQ on a missing one-off Gulf dividend and higher dividend taxes at Bharti holding level. Full-year OpCo EBIT growth guidance raised to mid-to-high single digits. 1H dividend +10% YoY.
Thai Life 3Q26 reported: VoNB THB1,486mn (+3% YoY), APE -19%, VoNB margin 54.7%, new business CSM THB2.4bn (-4% YoY), net profit -19% YoY, core profit -9% YoY, 9M26 core profit +2% YoY.
Atour Lifestyle 3Q26 beat and raised full-year revenue guidance (per Citi's 10 Nov note). Management expects a stable 4Q26E trend.
NAURA 3Q26 revenue growth was slower on a component shortage. Management expects 4Q26 growth to accelerate significantly. 9M26 new orders +60% YoY.
BYD: Citi expects 4Q26E wholesales above 1.5mn units (forecast), against October wholesales of 490k (reported).
risk_factors: Disruption to Nvidia's long-term architecture and supplier coordination could complicate the outlook from 2028 onward.
Possible increase in US scrutiny of Nvidia's Singapore sales, and further US export restrictions on Southeast Asia, could lead to Nvidia order cuts.
A slowdown in spec migration would cut pricing upside for Taiwan PCB and laminate suppliers.
BYD faces a lower export tax rebate and a higher battery consumption tax.
Eicher: commodity costs remain elevated and only 50% of cost pressure has been passed through.
vol_and_positioning: Fund flows, week of 11 November 2026: equity funds US$98.3bn inflow, bond funds near zero. US ETFs +US$66.1bn, global ETFs +US$15.4bn, European ETFs +US$2.5bn. Japan ETFs +US$20.8bn over 4 weeks.
geopolitical: Citi flags possible US national security tightening and scrutiny of Nvidia's Singapore sales, and a risk of further US export restrictions on Southeast Asia.
China's reduced export tax rebate (4%) and battery consumption tax hike (2%) affect BYD.
